Check the agreement of the best BLAST hits

Source: R/blast_hits.R
check_hits.Rd

For each query sequence, orders its hits by rank_by, decides whether the best ones agree on the taxon (Check ID) and summarises all of them.

The hits are ordered by rank_by (Similarity score, identity or bitscore) and then by identity, coverage, bitscore and BLAST order. Hits within tolerance of the best value are "at best": they are tied candidates for the identification.

Check ID looks at the first check_n hits and compares only the ones at best: a hit clearly worse than the best one is most likely another taxon, not a competing identification.

  • "best ID": all the hits at best among the first check_n have the taxid of the first hit.

  • "check ID": some of them has another taxid or an unknown one (0 or empty, as in databases built without a taxid map).

  • NA: no hits.

The other columns use all the hits of the sequence: N hits, N taxids (distinct known taxids), N hits same taxid as 1st, N hits at best, N taxids at best, Taxids at best (the known taxids of the hits at best, in rank order, separated by ";", for a lowest common ancestor) and At best truncated (TRUE when the last subject BLAST returned is at best: more tied subjects may exist beyond search_alignments; NA when search_alignments is unknown).

With an informative column (see uninformative_references()), all of this is computed among the informative hits, or among all the hits when a query has no informative one (and then Check ID is "check ID"). N uninformative counts the other hits and Best uninformative score is the best value of rank_by among them: above the best informative hit, the query is closer to an uncultured or environmental sequence than to any named organism (a sign of a taxon missing from the database).

Usage

check_hits(
  hits,
  check_n = 10L,
  tolerance = 0.5,
  rank_by = c("similarity", "identity", "bitscore"),
  search_alignments = NA_integer_
)

Arguments

hits

Data frame with one row per hit and the columns query, identity, staxid and, as needed by rank_by, qcovhsp or bitscore. The BLAST order is taken from blast_rank or rank, or else from the row order. Optional: informative (logical).

check_n

Number of best hits used by Check ID.

tolerance

Difference from the best value, in the units of rank_by (points of Similarity score or identity, bits of bitscore), under which hits are tied.

rank_by

Criterion to order the hits: "similarity" (Similarity score, see similarity_score()), "identity" or "bitscore".

search_alignments

Number of subjects BLAST was asked for, to compute At best truncated.

Value

A tibble with query and the summary columns.

Examples

hits <- data.frame(
  query = "q1", identity = c(100, 99, 98.7), qcovhsp = 100,
  staxid = c("9606", "9598", "9597")
)
check_hits(hits)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 11
#>   query `Check ID` `N hits` `N taxids` N hits same taxid as 1…¹ `N hits at best`
#>   <chr> <chr>         <int>      <int>                    <int>            <int>
#> 1 q1    best ID           3          3                        1                1
#> # ℹ abbreviated name: ¹​`N hits same taxid as 1st`
#> # ℹ 5 more variables: `N taxids at best` <int>, `Taxids at best` <chr>,
#> #   `At best truncated` <lgl>, `N uninformative` <int>,
#> #   `Best uninformative score` <dbl>
